claims.claim: The US treaty credit covers only the 15% US tax on dividends, so for someone in a 15% US bracket dividends cost about 5% more

sources.name: IRS: US–South Africa income tax convention (text)
sources.says: Effective 1 January 1998. Article 10(2)(b): source-country tax on portfolio dividends may not exceed "15 per cent of the gross amount". Article 23(2)(a): where a US citizen is resident in South Africa, South Africa "shall allow as a credit against South African tax, only the tax paid, if any, that the United States may impose under the provisions of this Convention, other than taxes that may be imposed solely by reason of citizenship"; 23(2)(b)–(c): the US then credits the South African tax left after that credit, without reducing the US tax creditable in South Africa. Read from the PDF that WebFetch saved, its text streams decompressed locally.

sources.name: PwC: South Africa, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 29 May 2026. "Most other foreign dividends are subject to tax at an effective rate of 20%." "Interest received by or accrued to an individual is taxable"; the exemption (ZAR 23,800, or 34,500 at 65+) is for local interest. 40% of net capital gains are taxed at normal rates: "The maximum effective tax rate on capital gains is 18%."

claims.note: Article 23(2) limits South Africa's credit for a US citizen-resident to the tax the treaty lets the US charge a non-citizen (15% on portfolio dividends, Article 10(2)(b)); the remaining South African tax (20% − 15% = 5%) is due, and the US credits it only without going below its own 15%. The "about 5%" is that arithmetic.

sources.name: SAIT compendium (2016): Income Tax Act, Eighth Schedule paragraph 24
sources.says: 2016 compendium. Paragraph 24(1): "The base cost of an asset, other than an asset situated in the Republic listed in paragraph 2 (1) (b) (i) and (ii)" "acquired by a person before the date on which that person became a resident is the sum of the value of that asset" under subparagraph (2) or (3) plus later allowable expenditure, so gains before residence are outside the tax.

claims.claim: Local medical schemes cannot refuse on age but add a late-joiner penalty of up to 75% of the contribution for someone with no prior South African cover

sources.name: Discovery Health Medical Scheme: underwriting policies and protocols (2026)
sources.says: 2026 edition. "The Scheme is an open medical scheme and is community-rated", with the same contributions "regardless of age (late-joiner penalties will affect the risk portion of contributions) or health status". A late joiner is 35 or older with no South African scheme membership ("schemes and insurance policies from other countries are not recognised"); penalty by years not a member after 35: 1–4 years 5%, 5–14 years 25%, 15–24 years 50%, "25 years and more 75%", added to the risk contribution only, not the savings account. Read from the PDF that WebFetch saved, its text streams decompressed locally.

claims.note: Discovery's rules say it is an open, community-rated scheme and the penalty applies to the risk portion of the contribution; "cannot refuse on age" rests on that (the Medical Schemes Act itself was not read).
